title: Conquer Your Anger
coreMove: Treat anger as a hot draft instead of an order: write it, wait, then check whether justice or pride is speaking before you answer in public or in private.

exampleSpecs.audience: two leads facing the same angry customer thread
exampleSpecs.stakes: one reply repairs the issue while the other spreads damage
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Two different people face the same provocation, one using Lincoln's unsent-letter delay and one sending in heat.

exampleSpecs.domain: peer coaching before a vendor review
exampleSpecs.audience: Bryce preparing to confront damaged work
exampleSpecs.stakes: truth could become a performance of wounded pride
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: A peer reframes Bryce's anger with one quotable sentence before the review call.

exampleSpecs.audience: Ming learning to separate anger from justice
exampleSpecs.stakes: a student could confuse rage with moral seriousness
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: The learner's confusion becomes the teaching material: injury, pride, and response are sorted apart.

exampleSpecs.audience: Brandon changing the way he answers a provocation
exampleSpecs.stakes: a recurring family argument could be changed by one pause
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: The same person and table appear before and after adopting Lincoln's unsent-letter practice.

exampleSpecs.audience: Ephrem reviewing prior messages for the hidden pattern
exampleSpecs.stakes: the team may blame tone while missing the timing detail
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Review existing files and discover that timing, not vocabulary alone, predicted damage.

exampleSpecs.audience: Janet noticing wrong turns inside her own anger
exampleSpecs.stakes: a fair correction could become a character attack
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: No external dialogue; Janet's thought sequence moves from wrong turns to a cleaner response.
